# Native text-transform evidence

These original fixtures are generated by `tools/shape_text_transform_fixture.py`
with python-docx (MIT), lxml (BSD) and the repository's original XML helpers.
No corpus content or font binaries are redistributed. Arial is supplied by the
test computer. The reference application produces the reference PDFs.

Each source has 16 pages: superscript, subscript, raised/lowered text, combined
raised superscript, a raised superscript space with character spacing, and
50%/150% text width, first standalone and then in a 2x-coordinate group.
The two sources differ in `noAutofit` versus `spAutoFit`. All use compatibility
mode 15 and 20pt text inside the shape.

`tools/shape_text_transform_reference.py` pins source/PDF hashes and records
native fill bounds, text origins, text matrices, PDF font sizes and RGB hashes
of each shape rectangle. The reference application emits grouped width-scaled test glyphs as artwork
rather than extractable text; their appearance remains available in the PDF
and raster hash. Those glyphs must be visually checked, not treated as absent.

The native controls expose an existing shared-renderer limitation: The reference application's
Arial superscript is approximately 65% in both dimensions, whereas the current
renderer uses a Noto-derived 65% horizontal / 60% vertical transform for every
font. Native 20pt superscript is emitted at 12.96pt; the current preview paints
at 12pt vertically. The former combined raised-script line-allocation error is
fixed by reserving the declared font's metrics independently of script ink.
Font-specific glyph sizing and offsets remain unresolved.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.2.42 (`vertAlign`), 17.3.2.24 (`position`), and
17.3.2.43 (`w`) govern these run properties. `vertAlign` preserves the declared
font size while reducing and repositioning its displayed text; it does not
prescribe the exact scale factor. Positive `position` raises text in half-point
units without changing font size. The numerical native behavior is compatibility
evidence, not a normative scale supplied by the standard.

Both sources pass transitional schema validation (16 XML checks). The browser
tests open all 32 pages as editable and compare frames and surrounding text
baselines with the reference application within 0.2pt, including body edit/export/reopen and exact
undo/package preservation. Retained shapes now use the same script, position
and width transforms as body text. These tests do not certify script glyph
fidelity. Corpus source 114 remains partial, next blocked by pattern fills.
